title: "Dataframes: a table you can plot"

*A complex data type worth knowing exists. Used inside the back-half projects, not as a lecture.*

::: {.callout-note}
## Draft stub — planned contents
A deliberately light introduction. Presents a dataframe as a complex data type, introduced by doing as list and dict were: read_csv hands back an object, the object has columns you can pull out, and the whole thing can be handed to a plotting call or to the iplot widget to get a picture. Nothing about indexing, grouping, or joining is promised. Shows the apply pattern as the bridge from a small function the student wrote and tested to the library running it across every row, which is where authored code and library amplification meet. Real data analysis is explicitly out of scope; matplotlib and the iplot widget appear so students see graphics, text, and code blend on one notebook page.
:::
